tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

attachment.cliPrefix: You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- courier:changeset-analyzer: Delegate to this subagent when you need changeset@2 artifacts produced from a git diff. Input is a git diff, optionally a linked spec@1, and optionally smith's criteria_evidence from the TDD run that produced this diff. A diff spanning multiple independent topics produces one changeset@2 per topic, never one bundled entry — see judgment for how topics are distinguished. For each topic, classifies consumer_impact (behavior-change, new-capability, internal-only) and semver_impact (major, minor, patch, none) per shared/references/delivery/changesets.md's decision table, identifies that topic's own changed files, detects breaking changes, and maps acceptance_criteria IDs. Uses smith's criteria_evidence directly when supplied; otherwise reconstructs best-effort file-level evidence from the diff. Summary detail scales with semver_impact — terse for patch/internal-only, full old-to-new-to-required-action detail for major. Output is one or more changeset@2 objects conforming to shared/schemas/changeset@2.json, routed to pr-narrator or release-summarizer. (Tools: All tools)

- courier:commit-analyzer: Delegate to this subagent when the user has staged git changes and needs a conventional commit message written. Input is the staged diff. The agent reads shared/references/delivery/commits.md for type and scope conventions. Output is a JSON object containing commit_message, type (feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore, perf, ci, or build), scope (or null), a breaking flag, and a reasoning scratchpad. The commit message explains why the change was made, not what changed — the diff already shows what changed. The reasoning field is a private scratchpad explaining type and scope selection; it is not forwarded downstream. (Tools: All tools)

- courier:pr-narrator: Delegate to this subagent when the user needs a pull request title and body written for a set of staged or committed changes. Input is a git diff and optionally a linked spec@1 or requirement@1. The agent reads the PR template from shared/references/delivery/github.md and writes from the reviewer's perspective — what does a reviewer with zero prior context need to know to approve this confidently? Output is a JSON object with title, body, labels, and a reasoning scratchpad. The body covers what changed, why it was needed, and how to verify correctness. It explains the change's purpose, not a summary of the diff. Labels are inferred from the change type. (Tools: All tools)

- courier:release-summarizer: Delegate to this subagent when you need a release-artifact@2 generated from a collection of changeset@2 entries. Input is a list of changeset@2 JSON objects, the prior released version string, and a release date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Each input changeset already carries consumer_impact and semver_impact, set at authoring time by changeset-analyzer — this agent does not re-derive them. It filters out consumer_impact: internal-only entries, computes the release version as max(semver_impact) across the remaining changesets applied to the prior version, and carries each changeset's summary through as-is (already written in consumer-facing language at the right detail level). All breaking_changes strings from all input changesets are aggregated into the top-level breaking_changes array. Output is a release-artifact@2 conforming to shared/schemas/release-artifact@2.json. (Tools: All tools)

- courier:review-preprocessor: Delegate to this subagent before a PR is opened, to assemble the complete review package for the reviewer. Input is the changeset diff, optionally a linked spec@1 or requirement@1, test results, and any open questions the author wants answered. The agent bundles these into a structured review package — diff summary, linked spec reference, test result summary, and open questions list — so the reviewer has everything in one place before they start. Mechanical assembly only; no judgment about the change. Output is a JSON object with diff_summary, linked_spec, test_results, open_questions, and a reasoning scratchpad. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- mason:auditor: Delegate to this subagent to audit a plugin directory for ecosystem conformance. Check manifests, declared files, agent structure, prompt-prefix identity, routing, contracts, instruction economy, runtime reference quality, and shared linkage. Use repository validators for deterministic checks. Treat length as a review signal; fail prose only with evidence of filler, repetition, mixed rules, unsupported absolutes, or missing refutation. Read-only. Return a structured report. (Tools: All tools)

- mason:evaluation-adjudicator: Independently compare a completed isolated workflow run with its hidden fixture oracle and live evidence. Return `harness-evaluation@2` without prose scoring. (Tools: All tools)
- mason:evaluation-runner: Run one fixed behavioral fixture in an isolated workspace without reading its answer key. Return `evaluation-run@1` for independent adjudication. (Tools: All tools)

- mason:scaffolder: Delegate when creating a plugin or adding one agent to an existing plugin. Generate conformant manifests, skills, agents, routing, and shared linkage for the requested scope. Copy the constitution byte-for-byte. Return a JSON report of created files. (Tools: All tools)

- mason:schema-designer: Delegate to this subagent when the user wants to design a new JSON Schema for an inter-agent artifact — a structured payload passed between producers and consumers in the plugin ecosystem. Provide a description of what the artifact represents, who produces it, and who consumes it. The designer produces a JSON Schema following ecosystem conventions (draft 2020-12, $id as name@version, all fields documented, reasoning scratchpad field always present, additionalProperties false, required fields listed), checks for conflicts with existing schemas in shared/schemas/, and returns the schema object with a recommended filename. (Tools: All tools)

- muse:auditor: Delegate to this subagent when you need adversarial quality review of a component spec@1 before it enters planning. Input is a spec@1 JSON object describing a UI component. Checks for completeness: missing interactive states (hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty), missing accessibility criteria (role, name, focus order, keyboard operability, live-region or state-announcement behavior), invalid prop combinations not marked as error cases, ambiguous phrasing, scope overlap with other component specs, and unnecessary prose that costs every downstream reader without adding a needed fact. For every issue, produces the rewritten fix, not just a description. Output is a JSON object with an issues array (criterion_id, type, description, suggested_fix) and an overall pass/fail verdict. Standard: can a developer implement this component without one clarifying question? Does not check the spec against source artifacts — that's a verification concern; this checks whether the spec, on its own terms, is complete, unambiguous, and implementable. (Tools: All tools)

- muse:drafter: Delegate to this subagent when you have a completed requirement@1 (or free-text design intent) and need a formal component spec@1 drafted. Input is a requirement@1 and optionally design references (mockup description, existing component family, design-system tokens). Output is a spec@1 conforming to shared/schemas/spec@1.json: id (SPEC-NNN), purpose, scope, non_goals (at least one), acceptance_criteria (at least one), optional api_surface for the component's props. Every criterion must be falsifiable — confirmable by a tester with no implementation knowledge, using only observable behavior: rendered output, focus order, ARIA attributes, emitted events. Props, variants, every interactive state (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty), and accessibility criteria are each named explicitly. Error cases and invalid prop combinations carry is_error_case: true. Unknowns go in non_goals or reasoning — no TBDs anywhere. The muse orchestrator writes the spec to disk after exit-gate passes; this agent returns the spec object only. Also runs in correction mode: given spec_file_path, a criterion_id, and implementer's contradiction report, revises the affected criterion (and any dependent ones) and returns the full corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. (Tools: All tools)

- muse:exit-gate: Delegate to this subagent when a component spec@1 needs a definitive pass/fail judgment before entering the planning phase. Input is a spec@1 JSON object describing a UI component. This is an adversarial gatekeeper — the default disposition is fail, and the spec must earn a pass. The spec passes only if all four conditions hold: every acceptance criterion is a testable proposition with no vague language, no TBDs remain anywhere in the document, error cases and invalid prop combinations are explicitly covered with is_error_case: true criteria, and every interactive state and accessibility criterion (role, name, focus order, keyboard operability) implied by the component's props is present. On fail, every blocker is specific enough for the drafter to make a targeted fix without further clarification. Output is a verdict@1 conforming to shared/schemas/verdict@1.json with artifact_type set to spec@1. This agent is the binding exit gate — its fail verdict halts progression to navigator until the spec is corrected and resubmitted. Maximum 3 retries before escalation to a human reviewer. (Tools: All tools)

- navigator:challenger: Delegate to this subagent when a plan@1 needs adversarial review before implementation. Input is a plan@1 and its source spec@1. Check missing work, dependency order, prescription, batching, error handling, criterion coverage, and interface siblings against live evidence. Return per-issue repairs and a binding pass or fail verdict. (Tools: All tools)

- navigator:estimator: Delegate to this subagent when a plan@1 exists and you need a rough effort estimate before committing to execution. Input is a plan@1 JSON object. The agent produces a per-task time estimate in minutes, marks each task as parallelizable or sequential, lists blocking dependencies by task ID, and produces a total_minutes sum with explicit assumptions. The implementer is assumed to have full codebase context but no domain knowledge of the feature being built. A task is marked parallelizable only if it has no dependency on any other task in the current plan. All assumptions affecting the estimate are listed explicitly in an assumptions array. Output is a JSON object with total_minutes, a tasks array, and assumptions. (Tools: All tools)

- navigator:planner: Delegate to this subagent when you have a completed spec@1 and need a sequenced, executable implementation plan. Input is a spec@1 (or its spec_file_path, read from disk if provided). Output is a plan@1 conforming to shared/schemas/plan@1.json, with spec_file_path and spec_hash propagated from the spec. Decomposes into dependency-ordered tasks (foundational types, then logic, then integration); each task includes exact file paths, a brief implementation approach, exact implementation code as a concrete baseline (smith's implementer may improve on its shape, not its scope), the exact tests proving each criterion it covers, the verification command, a commit message, and covers_criteria naming every acceptance criterion it addresses. Every criterion must appear in some task's covers_criteria. Each task is one independently reviewable unit of change, sized to its Subsystem Batch's compilation boundary rather than a clock-time estimate; no TBDs. Also runs in amend mode: given an existing plan@1, a corrected spec@1, and the changed criterion_ids, patches only the affected tasks (adding new ones for newly introduced criteria) and leaves the rest untouched. Route output to challenger. (Tools: All tools)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- ranger:adversary: Invoke once per candidate after scanner and, for T7 or T10, boundary tracing. Try to refute reachability from current code and return `candidate-assessment@1`. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:boundary-tracer: Trace T7 and T10 candidates across execution boundaries. Supports Rust, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Go. Return `field-survival-map@1`. (Tools: All tools)
- ranger:exit-gate: Independently verify remediated `finding-report@2` entries and their defect families against current code. Return `verdict@3`. (Tools: All tools)

- ranger:recon: Invoke before scanning. Detect affected languages, trace reachable files from live entry points, and inventory project capabilities and current workspace state. Return `workspace-manifest@1`; do not judge defects. (Tools: All tools)

- ranger:scanner: Invoke after recon. Load the hazard pack for each scoped language, scan only live files, and emit every matching `candidate@1` without verdicting. Supports Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, and Go. (Tools: All tools)

- scribe:arch-auditor: Delegate to this subagent when a draft spec@1 needs checking against the workspace's whole-system architecture before it enters scribe/gate-spec — not against another spec, and not against a single function's signature, but against module boundaries, canonical abstractions, and invariants that span the codebase. Input is a spec@1 draft plus workspace_root. Default (check) mode: reads the persisted arch-model@2 at docs/architecture/model.json (or notes it is absent), reads broadly enough across the workspace to confirm the model still reflects reality, and checks the spec against it — flagging boundary violations (a dependency running the wrong direction), competing abstractions (a new type reinventing something the model already canonicalizes), and invariant conflicts. Output is an arch-audit@1 conforming to shared/schemas/arch-audit@1.json. Build mode: given no usable model or an explicit refresh request, reads the codebase broadly and produces or updates an arch-model@2 conforming to shared/schemas/arch-model@2.json — module boundaries, canonical abstractions, and invariants (each citing its governing decision record when one exists), the latter cumulative across everything scribe/architect has ever fixed. This agent does not patch specs or code — it reports fit, or builds the model fit is checked against. (Tools: All tools)

- scribe:architect: Delegate when `finding-report@2`, `implementation-review@2`, or `implementation-result@1` identifies a structural defect class. Inspect the live semantic model and persisted architecture, then produce a `spec@1` that makes recurrence impossible or machine-detectable. (Tools: All tools)

- scribe:auditor: Delegate to this subagent when you need adversarial quality review of a spec@1 before it enters planning. Input is a spec@1 JSON object. Checks seven dimensions: untestable/vague criteria, ambiguous phrasing, missing error cases, scope overlap with other specs, TBDs/incomplete sections, unnecessary prose that costs every downstream reader without adding a needed fact, and a field this spec introduces or changes on a type that another spec persists, serializes, or transmits with no matching round-trip criterion on the far side and no note that the gap is intentional. For every issue, produces the rewritten fix, not just a description. Output is a JSON object with an issues array (criterion_id, type, description, suggested_fix) and an overall pass/fail verdict. Standard: can a developer implement this spec without one clarifying question? Does not check the spec against source artifacts — that's verifier's role; this checks whether the spec, on its own terms, is complete, unambiguous, and implementable. (Tools: All tools)

- scribe:drafter: Delegate to this subagent when you have a completed requirement@1 and need a formal spec@1 drafted. Input is a requirement@1 and optionally a research-report@1. Output is a spec@1 conforming to shared/schemas/spec@1.json: id (SPEC-NNN), purpose, scope, non_goals (at least one), acceptance_criteria (at least one), optional api_surface. Every criterion must be falsifiable — confirmable by a tester with no implementation knowledge, using only observable behavior. Error cases carry is_error_case: true. Unknowns go in non_goals or reasoning — no TBDs anywhere. The scribe orchestrator writes the spec to disk after exit-gate passes; this agent returns the spec object only. Also runs in correction mode: given spec_file_path, a criterion_id, and implementer's contradiction report, revises the affected criterion (and any dependent ones) and returns the full corrected spec@1 with revision_note set. (Tools: All tools)

- scribe:drift-checker: On-demand diagnostic: given a spec_file_path and a workspace root, verifies the current code still implements every acceptance criterion in the spec. Reads the spec from disk, not from context, and reads implementation/tests from the workspace. When a prior changeset@2's criteria_evidence is available, uses its pointers as a starting point but re-verifies each one — code may have moved since it was recorded. Classifies each criterion as covered (implementation and tests match the contract), uncovered (nothing found), or drifted (behavior diverges from the criterion). Not a blocking gate — exit-gate is. Use for ongoing maintenance, detecting drift weeks or months after implementation. Output is a drift report with covered/uncovered/drifted arrays plus a summary. (Tools: All tools)

- scribe:exit-gate: Issue the binding `verdict@3` for a `spec@1` before planning. Pass only when every criterion is testable, error behavior is explicit, no TBD remains, scope fits one planning cycle, and all checks are complete. (Tools: All tools)

- scribe:verifier: Delegate to this subagent when you need to verify that a draft spec@1 is grounded in its source artifacts — the requirement@1 and optional research-report@1 — before it proceeds to auditing or gating. Input is a spec@1 draft plus the originating requirement@1 and any research-report@1 used to produce it. For each acceptance criterion, the agent checks whether the requirement or research report supplies evidence that the criterion is necessary and correctly scoped. Each criterion is classified as supported (evidence found with a direct citation), unsupported (criterion appears with no basis in the source artifacts), or overfitted (criterion is narrower than the source supports, excluding valid cases). The agent collects evidence only and does not produce a pass/fail verdict. Output is a structured evidence report with supported, unsupported, and overfitted arrays plus a reasoning scratchpad. For post-implementation drift checking, use drift-checker instead. (Tools: All tools)
- sentinel:exit-gate: Issue `verdict@3` from a completed verification report. Separate blockers, coverage gaps, and pending checks; pass only within the verified scope. (Tools: All tools)

- sentinel:recon: Delegate to this subagent at the start of the sentinel gate protocol when an artifact must be inventoried before verification begins. Input is an artifact path or description. The agent determines the artifact type, locates it in the workspace, enumerates the criteria it must be verified against (derived from a linked spec or requirement, or from the artifact's own acceptance criteria section if none is linked), and identifies source files to cross-check during verification. This is purely mechanical discovery — the agent produces no pass/fail opinion. Output is a JSON manifest with artifact_type, artifact_path, criteria array, source_files array, and a reasoning scratchpad. Do not delegate here for judgment; route the manifest to verifier for criterion cross-reference. (Tools: All tools)

- sentinel:verifier: Delegate to this subagent after recon has produced its artifact manifest, and before any final verdict is issued. Input is the recon manifest from recon, including the artifact path, criteria list, and source files. The agent reads the artifact and each source file and, for each criterion, collects concrete evidence that confirms or refutes it. Each criterion is classified as verified (positive evidence found), failed (evidence contradicts the criterion), or unverifiable (requires external context not accessible). Absence of a counter-example is not sufficient to classify a criterion as verified. This agent is a neutral evidence collector — it does not issue verdicts. Output is a JSON object with verified, failed, and unverifiable arrays. Route output to exit-gate for the final verdict. (Tools: All tools)

- smith:exit-gate: Delegate after all planned batches have terminal results and approved `implementation-review@2` artifacts. Verify current code, scoped evidence, sibling completeness, and pending work independently. Return `verdict@3`. (Tools: All tools)

- smith:implementer: Delegate to execute one plan task. Read persisted criteria, design and implement the change, prove it with tests, and record exact evidence. Commit only when the caller supplies `commit_authorized: true`; otherwise return a null commit SHA. Report spec contradictions or architecture needs instead of forcing a pass. Scope is one task. (Tools: All tools)

- smith:mutator: Delegate after implementation. Use available project-native mutation tooling against changed behavior, or a controlled deliberate fault when appropriate. Analyze survivors and return `mutation-report@2`; unavailable tooling becomes a coverage gap. (Tools: All tools)

- smith:recon: Delegate before implementation. Inspect current workspace state, affected languages, entry points, project-native verification capabilities, baseline tests, and persisted artifact freshness. Return `workspace-manifest@1`; stop on a failing baseline. (Tools: All tools)

- smith:reviewer: Delegate after an implementation batch and discrimination check. Review scope, verification fit, related defects, semantic models, and architecture. Return `implementation-review@2`; route structural families to `scribe:architect`. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vanguard:reader: Delegate to this subagent after recon produces a source map. Input is the source map from recon plus the original research question. The agent reads every identified source and extracts findings relevant to the question, with a citation, confidence level (confirmed, likely, or assumed), and source attribution for each. Does not synthesize or recommend — extracts faithfully from what it reads. Sources that cannot be read are noted as unreadable rather than skipped. Output is a JSON object containing a findings array, a sources_read list, and a reasoning scratchpad noting contradictions or surprises. Do not skip any source from the map; recon already filtered for relevance. Route output to synthesizer. (Tools: All tools)

- vanguard:recon: Delegate to this subagent at the start of any research task, before any reading or analysis begins. Input is a requirement@1 or free-text research question. For each risk it produces a description, severity (critical, high, medium, or low), likelihood, a concrete trigger condition describing when the risk materializes, and a mitigation sketch. Input is unstructured text only; no schema is required from the caller. The agent infers id, statement, stakeholder, why, and done_when from the provided text without asking any clarifying questions. Fields that cannot be inferred are omitted; gaps are noted in the reasoning scratchpad. The out_of_scope field is intentionally left empty — populating it is the clarifier's responsibility. Output is a flat requirement@1 JSON object conforming to shared/schemas/requirement@1.json. Every done_when criterion must be a testable proposition verifiable from outside the implementation. Route this output directly to clarifier before writing a spec. (Tools: All tools)
- weaver:prioritizer: Delegate to this subagent when a set of requirement@1 drafts needs ranking before planning starts. Input is a list of requirement@1 objects. The agent ranks them by impact (who is affected and how badly), urgency (signals in why/done_when indicating time pressure), and dependency order (a requirement that another depends on ranks above the one depending on it, regardless of its own impact/urgency score). Output is an ordered list with a stated rationale per requirement, plus any dependency relationships found. Does not modify requirement@1 objects — ranking and rationale only. (Tools: All tools)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

# Draft work packages (WP) — v0, to be extended by unmapped findings

Plugins: courier, mason, muse, navigator, ranger, scribe, sentinel, smith, vanguard, weaver (+ shared/, docs/adr, harnesses/codex).

## G0 Defects and baselines
- WP-01 Fix muse's dangling "ranger accessibility hazard taxonomy" references (plugin.json, README, SKILL.md) — either build the pack (WP-44) or correct the docs.
- WP-02 Migrate muse from verdict@1 to verdict@3 (version bump, Codex counterpart).
- WP-03 Baseline metrics script over transcripts: gate rounds per spec, blocker types (wording vs substantive), time-to-first-visual, post-gate defects, stalls/failed agent tasks, tokens/cost per phase.
- WP-04 Cross-reference link checker in `just check` / mason:audit-plugin (plugin docs referencing things that don't exist).
- WP-05 Correct/verify factual claims in repo docs touched by this evaluation (counts, tier tables).

## G1 Exploration and ideation
- WP-10 ADR(s): exploratory/divergent cognitive mode (amends ADR 003), mode routing, non-binding artifacts.
- WP-11 muse `sketch` skill: option files with stable IDs + status (open/parked/chosen/rejected) + one-line reason; anchor brief re-derived each round; ~3 options default; TBDs allowed; no gate; visibly low-fidelity marker; assumptions list; hard stop before implementation; scratch-dir-only write guard.
- WP-12 Sketch rendering medium and option matrix: local dev server/static pages, Playwright screenshots, side-by-side option boards, brand × theme × viewport matrix from tokens; Artifacts as optional; how sketches land in a repo.
- WP-13 Decision log + cross-session persistence: format, where it lives in consumer repos, surfaced through AGENTS.md routing, retrieval of prior-session decisions, "recorded but not applied" detection, rule candidates pending until human accepts (never promote a single screenshot/comment), conflict with ADR table.
- WP-14 `promote` skill: prototype/sketch → requirement@1 → spec@2; prototype/screenshots kept as visual oracle; change-delta specs; carry decision_ref; resolve TBDs or move to non_goals.
- WP-15 smith `spike` skill: validate that a tool/library/approach works in the stack; throwaway marker; skip plan/spec/mutator/reviewer/exit-gate; report verified vs unverified; smoke-check evidence recipe; promote or discard.
- WP-16 Direction-commit and anti-slop controls: propose ~4 distinct directions → user picks; named aesthetic; ban lists; rejection clauses; second-order slop patterns; taste dials (variance/motion/density); deterministic slop scanner.
- WP-17 Visual critique / design-review agent: Playwright multi-viewport critic, severity tiers (P0–P3), user-impact language with screenshots, hierarchy/contrast checks; distinct from spec audit.
- WP-18 Mode router: shape / sketch / spike / implement / review / copy / harden / promote; exploration modes read-only or sketch-only; explicit authority labeling ("cleared by"); IFR/VFR framing; ability to enter/leave gated mode explicitly.
- WP-19 Exploration → hardening handoff: characterization tests, pin behavior, hardening checklist (empty/loading/error states, a11y, copy truth, responsive), "harden" mode keeps direction and fixes state/a11y.
- WP-20 Copy/voice workflow: copy review agent/skill, case-study truth audit, voice consistency, content provenance (see WP-43).
- WP-21 Research for design (vanguard): visual/competitive sourcing, prior-art boards, keep the recon→reader→synthesizer path that worked; framing questions sharply.

## G2 Spec and visual intent
- WP-30 ADR + `spec@2`: token references `{path}`, visual references (Figma node, Storybook story id, screenshot path), per-state render references, decision_ref, supersedes links; keep falsifiable criteria; no TBD in spec (TBD only in sketch).
- WP-31 Design-intent artifact: small routed files (DESIGN.md-compatible front matter tokens + prose + Do/Don't + rejection clauses), lint/export via optional CLI, `coverage-gaps` file, exemplar good/bad PRs; component facts via lookup not monolith.
- WP-32 Ground-truth extraction step (recon): tokens, props, measured geometry from repo/running page/prototype → facts file consumed by drafter/planner/verifier; compile examples (validate); version-tied reviews.
- WP-33 Reference tables loaded before drafting: ARIA APG patterns, keyboard maps, platform a11y APIs; "never write from memory" hard rule.
- WP-34 Human-reviewable spec rendering and approval evidence: dual format (JSON + readable), rendered approval boards, "show, don't describe" before approval.
- WP-35 Optional design-source adapter: design-source@1 (figma|screenshot|html|description|none); capability-detected Figma MCP adapter (metadata first, then node), Storybook MCP, Code Connect-equivalent checks (token use, component reuse), rules-file generator.
- WP-36 Spec/plan size and stall guards: size caps, chunked writes, split specs, supersession handling and stale-spec cleanup.

## G3 Verification evidence
- WP-40 ADR + workspace-manifest@2: capability kinds browser/visual/a11y/storybook/e2e; unrendered UI is a coverage gap, never a pass; keeps ADR 005 (artifact-agnostic gate).
- WP-41 render-evidence artifact: screenshots per viewport/theme/state, axe/Lighthouse JSON, console errors, a11y-tree snapshots; baseline approval before it becomes a baseline.
- WP-42 Deterministic UI checks: token lint (hardcoded values), computed-style checks, contrast/target-size/reflow probes, landmarks, JS size budget; state that automated a11y coverage is partial.
- WP-43 Copy-provenance check: rendered text vs source copy; invented stats/names/testimonials; quoted evidence + location per finding.
- WP-44 ranger accessibility hazard pack for TSX/CSS (or removal of references, see WP-01).
- WP-45 Visual-regression + CI placement policy: Playwright/Storybook/axe in CI, behavior-vs-CSS testing policy, baseline approval, Chromatic/Percy/Lost Pixel options.
- WP-46 smith UI verification recipe: component/DOM testing, Storybook interaction/a11y tests, Playwright; mutation limits for markup/CSS; sibling review for UI.
- WP-47 UI "code intelligence" query layer (computed styles, a11y tree, token usage, component usage) extending the language-service evidence guidance (commit f10e6b8).

## G4 Gates and orchestration
- WP-50 Gate-hygiene constitution amendment: evidence-citing blockers, "no findings" is a valid pass, mechanical fixes outside the gate, convergence control for wording-only blockers, scanners report all with confidence/severity then filter separately.
- WP-51 Retry-cap enforcement with real human escalation; overrides declared and logged (no silent "owner-directed gate pass").
- WP-52 Readback in the correction loop; shared-contract-first step for sibling specs; cross-spec contradiction checks up front.
- WP-53 Standard vocabulary and fixed urgency tiers (affirm/negative/unable/standby/verify/correction/wilco/say again; P0–P3 definitions).
- WP-54 Stall/lost-contact procedures: per-agent timeouts, fallbacks, go-around, chunked writes.
- WP-55 Orchestrator owns subagent spawning; no agent spawns its own verifiers; spawn caps; file-ownership declaration in plans; single writer for shared tokens/config; merge one branch at a time; post-merge render check; ceiling 3–5 parallel agents.
- WP-56 Investigate why smith reviewer/mutator/exit-gate/recon and sentinel were never used in either project; integrate or simplify.
- WP-57 Repo-wide pre-commit gate cost during parallel smith runs: scoped checks guidance.
- WP-58 Plan quality: stale geometry, plan amendment when spec changes, challenger checks for contradictions with live code.

## G5 Prompt and agent design (model guidance)
- WP-60 mason:evaluate paired-eval harness: transcript replay first, then smoke, k=3, full; per-task medians + Wilcoxon; exclude failures from both arms; bill-based; outcome-graded; at actual effort.
- WP-61 `reasoning` field refusal test and decision (rename vs keep; 29 of 31 schemas; ADR 004 versioning).
- WP-62 Ablations of constitution/backstory/5-part skeleton (ADR 001/006).
- WP-63 Tier re-check: Haiku 5.5 recon, Opus 5.5 gates starting medium, Fable 5.1 trial, effort sweep, GPT-6 mapping.
- WP-64 Prescriptiveness audit: ration MUST/ALWAYS, explain "never X", remove "think carefully", remove qualitative filtering in producers, avoid over-verification in Opus producers, each harness component encodes an assumption.
- WP-65 Narration brevity ("be concise" for status/rationale/reports) evaluated vs baseline; not for specs/handoffs.
- WP-66 Context management: structured JSON state + progress notes + git; fresh context vs compaction; append-only history; no mid-session prompt/tool edits.
- WP-67 Skill-rule evals for the new design skills (hidden expected edits on unseen interfaces; shadcn/Vercel style).
- WP-68 Token-saver stance: paired test of rtk on the user's own workflow (optional, user config untouched).

## G6 Harness, Codex, AGENTS.md, distribution
- WP-70 Codex counterparts for every new skill/agent: outcome-first wording, boundaries, stop conditions, hierarchy, no effort `none`, TOML subagents, sandbox-enforced read-only, `just marketplace-sync`.
- WP-71 AGENTS.md strategy: short router, ≤32 KiB for Codex, one-line CLAUDE.md importing AGENTS.md, closest-file override, three layers (rules / lookup tool / AGENTS.md), constitution pointer.
- WP-72 Skills versioning and maintenance à la TanStack Intent: validate examples by compiling, review tied to source versions, mechanical repair vs judgment, CI checks that surface without auto-fixing, generate skills from source.
- WP-73 Drift: spec-drift extended to intent files, facts files and decision logs; docs freshness.
- WP-74 Lookup interface for design-system facts: CLI vs MCP, JSON over Markdown, llms.txt, component manifests.

## G7 Consumer-repo follow-ups (not plugin changes; recorded so they are not lost)
- WP-80 Add Playwright/Storybook/axe to CI, restore visual/a11y checks deferred on 13 Oct, screenshot assertions.
- WP-81 Duplicate/competing abstractions (orin vs twx packages, foundations/ui vs components, css() usage, brand branches), unported packages/rules.
- WP-82 Decision-status staleness, spec supersession cleanup, copy truth audit follow-ups, SEO checks.

## G8 Open research / verification items
- WP-90 Verify unverified claims and unread primary sources (OpenAI model pages 403, unfetched Anthropic engineering/Claude Code pages, uSpec repo, DESIGN.md agent integration docs, Figma specifics, ICAO documents).
- WP-91 Measure gate cost (tokens/time) from transcripts.

11	- Guide guidance: rules files = "onboarding notes", structure Figma w/ components, variables, semantic names, Auto Layout, annotations; break large selections up; Starter plan ~6 calls/month, paid seats per-minute REST Tier 1 limits. 12	- Write to canvas: https://www.figma.com/blog/the-figma-canvas-is-now-open-to-agents/ ; use_figma builds with real components/variables/auto layout; skills = markdown instruction sets (9 examples e.g. /figma-generate-library, /apply-design-system); free in beta, later usage-based; nondeterministic; roadmap: images, custom fonts.

16	- https://www.figma.com/blog/the-benefits-of-code-connect-in-mcp/ : without it agent fabricates components (Coinbase: stepper from progress bars). Median with CC: quality +1 (2->3 on 1-4 Likert), tokens -29.5%, duration -19.6%; scales with coverage. (A search snippet quoted different Coinbase numbers 11.5%/22.3%/22.5% - unverified, different source.)

23	- Pipeline: Figma variables -> DTCG JSON -> Style Dictionary -> CSS; Tokens Studio for bidirectional git sync (secondary: https://atomize.tools/blog/figma-design-tokens-vibe-coding/). Unverified in detail.

26	- LogRocket https://blog.logrocket.com/ux-design/design-to-code-with-figma-mcp/ : screenshots alone drift; messy layers hurt; no CC => regenerates components; output needed manual import/responsive fixes; exported token JSON helped.
27	- ByteByteGo https://blog.bytebytego.com/p/figma-design-to-code-code-to-design : 25k default MCP response cap; scan-first (get_metadata) then zoom in; each handoff lossy (logic/state lost both ways); capture walks DOM computed styles; agent tools vary.
28	- hipsquare https://blog.hipsquare.io/posts/2026-05-10-figma-playwright-mcp : Figma MCP + Playwright screenshot loop; claims ~50% time reduction on component sets (self-reported, small).
29	- Design Systems Collective (403 on fetch; snippet only) https://www.designsystemscollective.com/the-hidden-cost-of-figma-mcp-roundtripping-and-the-sustainable-model-i-use-instead-142d8e782a51 : token tax of roundtripping. UNVERIFIED content.
30	- Code-first: https://medium.com/@garimasadhnani/stop-making-figma-prototypes-how-i-build-live-ui-with-claude-code-and-mcps-fd5379f9072e ; https://medium.com/@karthikmulugu/i-let-claude-design-my-entire-website-using-shadcn-magic-ui-and-playwright-mcp-heres-what-ad24860b705b ; https://mowgli.ai/blog/claude-code-ui-design-workflow (snippets only, not read). Loop: implement -> screenshot -> diff list -> fix.
31	- Community skills: figma/mcp-server-guide figma-implement-design (https://claudemarketplaces.com/skills/figma/mcp-server-guide/figma-implement-design), figma-use, southleft/figma-console-mcp-skills (https://github.com/southleft/figma-console-mcp-skills), tempad-dev figma-design-to-code.
32	
33	## Wisp implications (my inference)
34	Integration points: (1) muse spec inputs: design reference as an optional typed artifact (design-source) w/ tokens/components/states; (2) smith verification: visual evidence step (screenshot + a11y snapshot) as a generic oracle, not Figma-specific; (3) token/component mapping check (tokens used vs hardcoded; existing component reuse = Code Connect analogue); (4) drift check (spec-drift for visual); (5) rules file generation.
35	Figma-optional: define design-source@1 with `kind: figma|screenshot|html|description|none`, normalize to {tokens, components, states, reference_images}. Figma adapter uses MCP if present; otherwise browser-screenshot loop against spec criteria. Capability-detect MCP tools, never require. Keep context cost low: metadata-first, per-node fetch. Treat Figma output as reference not truth (over-literal, absolute layout). Don't depend on write-to-canvas (beta, pricing changing).

1	# R3: AI-native design ideation tools (researched 2026-10-17)
2	
3	Confidence: web-search summaries plus two page fetches. Many sources are vendor or blog reviews, so treat as medium confidence. Tempo, Relume, Uizard and Bolt variant behavior are UNVERIFIED beyond one-line descriptions.
4	
5	## Per-tool
6	
7	### Claude Design (Anthropic)
8	- Options: ask in chat ("show me 2-3 alternative layouts"). The first generation is a starting point. Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design
9	- Steering: chat for structural change, inline comments on canvas elements, direct canvas editing (drag, resize, align), sliders for precision (https://uxpilot.ai/blogs/claude-design-review).
10	- Design system: ingests from a GitHub repo, design files, uploads, or a local codebase. Each system becomes an artifact reusable in Claude Code. It self-checks output against the system. Settings > Design Systems has a "Migrate team design systems" action.
11	- Handoff: export as .zip, PDF, PPTX, HTML, or Canva. Send-to integrations include v0, Lovable, Replit, Netlify, Miro and others. "Hand off to Claude Code" produces a bundle of design files, chat and a README with a paste-able prompt. A third-party description says the bundle holds a component structure spec, tokens used, layout hierarchy and assets (https://claudefa.st/blog/guide/mechanics/claude-design-handoff). That description is not first-party, so treat it as UNVERIFIED in detail. See also https://claude.com/product/design
12	- Explore then harden: no version history "yet". The workaround is to tell Claude "save what we have and try a completely different approach".
13	- Reported failures:
14	  - Inline comments sometimes vanish.
15	  - Multi-person editing is unreliable.
16	  - Weekly usage burn: PCWorld reportedly used 80% of a Pro week building three variations (https://uxpilot.ai/blogs/claude-design-review, https://flowstep.ai/blog/claude-design-review/).
17	  - Outputs drift by revision 4-5. Recovery is a fresh anchoring prompt, not stacked corrections.
18	  - Design-system copies drift out of sync with the real system. Some reviewers advise pasting tokens and specs into the prompt instead.
19	  - Output is "safe/template-y" (https://the-designengineer.com/insights/claude-design-review-is-it-worth-it/).
20	  - Annotations can only be seen by hovering over the chat comments.
21	
22	### Google Stitch
23	- "Ideate" mode is for early exploration and "Flash" is fast generation. Both generate multiple alternatives (https://uithings.com/what-is-google-stitch).
24	- The March 2026 update added an infinite canvas mixing images, code and UI, a design agent that remembers project history, voice, and instant prototypes (auto-generated missing screens). It also added an MCP server for Claude Code and Cursor (https://sfailabs.com/guides/google-stitch-vs-figma).
25	- Handoff: paste into Figma as layered Auto Layout; HTML/CSS/Tailwind export. Framework export (Vue, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI) is claimed by one source only: UNVERIFIED (https://vibecoding.app/blog/google-stitch-review).
26	- Positioning: ideate in Stitch, finish in Figma, then build in code.
27	
28	### v0 (Vercel)
29	- Design Mode is a visual editing panel. Design Systems 2.0 uses a shadcn registry to pass tokens and components to v0. Output for the same prompt shifts per imported system, which is relevant to brand/theme comparison (https://v0.app/docs/design-systems).
30	- Since March 2026, v0 infers the design system automatically instead of manual selection. Design Mode has reported instability (https://community.vercel.com/t/design-mode-changes-where-do-i-select-the-design-system/36398.md).
31	- Output is React code, so handoff is the code itself. Variant/branching UX: not verified.
32	
33	### Figma Make / Figma AI
34	- Make kits combine a React package or Figma library with guidelines, so prototypes use production components (https://www.figma.com/blog/introducing-make-kits-and-make-attachments/).
35	- The Figma agent claims to generate "explore multiple directions" variations using real components and tokens (https://www.figma.com/solutions/ai-design-iteration-generator/, marketing copy).
36	- Forum failure reports: changes confirmed but not applied, instructions ignored, stuck builds. Users have requested branching/version control for Make (https://forum.figma.com/suggest-a-feature-11/figma-make-structured-version-control-iteration-branching-for-ai-workflows-51303, https://forum.figma.com/report-a-problem-6/figma-make-not-following-even-simple-instructions-updates-not-occurring-46762).
37	
38	### Magic Patterns
39	- Infinite canvas. You duplicate a component and prompt for parallel variations, such as four headers in different styles compared side by side. It uses your own tokens and component library (https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/magic-patterns). This is the closest match to the option-board pattern.
40	
41	### Subframe
42	- Canvas plus coding agent. Layers map to HTML/React. Components with props, slots and variants sync to the codebase (https://uxmagic.ai/blog/magic-patterns-alternatives). Variant generation for ideation: UNVERIFIED.
43	
44	### Lovable, Bolt
45	- Both are full-app builders. Both have click-to-edit layers: Lovable Visual Edits (https://lovable.dev/blog/introducing-visual-edits), and Bolt Visual Edits, which stacks changes and sends them to the model in one batch (https://bolt.new/blog/visual-edits).
46	- Neither is primarily a divergent-exploration tool.
47

# R3: AI-native design ideation tools (researched 2026-10-17)

Confidence: web-search summaries plus two page fetches. Many sources are vendor or blog reviews, so treat as medium confidence. Tempo, Relume, Uizard and Bolt variant behavior are UNVERIFIED beyond one-line descriptions.

## Per-tool

### Claude Design (Anthropic)
- Options: ask in chat ("show me 2-3 alternative layouts"). The first generation is a starting point. Source: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14604416-get-started-with-claude-design
- Steering: chat for structural change, inline comments on canvas elements, direct canvas editing (drag, resize, align), sliders for precision (https://uxpilot.ai/blogs/claude-design-review).
- Design system: ingests from a GitHub repo, design files, uploads, or a local codebase. Each system becomes an artifact reusable in Claude Code. It self-checks output against the system. Settings > Design Systems has a "Migrate team design systems" action.
- Handoff: export as .zip, PDF, PPTX, HTML, or Canva. Send-to integrations include v0, Lovable, Replit, Netlify, Miro and others. "Hand off to Claude Code" produces a bundle of design files, chat and a README with a paste-able prompt. A third-party description says the bundle holds a component structure spec, tokens used, layout hierarchy and assets (https://claudefa.st/blog/guide/mechanics/claude-design-handoff). That description is not first-party, so treat it as UNVERIFIED in detail. See also https://claude.com/product/design
- Explore then harden: no version history "yet". The workaround is to tell Claude "save what we have and try a completely different approach".
- Reported failures:
  - Inline comments sometimes vanish.
  - Multi-person editing is unreliable.
  - Weekly usage burn: PCWorld reportedly used 80% of a Pro week building three variations (https://uxpilot.ai/blogs/claude-design-review, https://flowstep.ai/blog/claude-design-review/).
  - Outputs drift by revision 4-5. Recovery is a fresh anchoring prompt, not stacked corrections.
  - Design-system copies drift out of sync with the real system. Some reviewers advise pasting tokens and specs into the prompt instead.
  - Output is "safe/template-y" (https://the-designengineer.com/insights/claude-design-review-is-it-worth-it/).
  - Annotations can only be seen by hovering over the chat comments.

### Google Stitch
- "Ideate" mode is for early exploration and "Flash" is fast generation. Both generate multiple alternatives (https://uithings.com/what-is-google-stitch).
- The March 2026 update added an infinite canvas mixing images, code and UI, a design agent that remembers project history, voice, and instant prototypes (auto-generated missing screens). It also added an MCP server for Claude Code and Cursor (https://sfailabs.com/guides/google-stitch-vs-figma).
- Handoff: paste into Figma as layered Auto Layout; HTML/CSS/Tailwind export. Framework export (Vue, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI) is claimed by one source only: UNVERIFIED (https://vibecoding.app/blog/google-stitch-review).
- Positioning: ideate in Stitch, finish in Figma, then build in code.

### v0 (Vercel)
- Design Mode is a visual editing panel. Design Systems 2.0 uses a shadcn registry to pass tokens and components to v0. Output for the same prompt shifts per imported system, which is relevant to brand/theme comparison (https://v0.app/docs/design-systems).
- Since March 2026, v0 infers the design system automatically instead of manual selection. Design Mode has reported instability (https://community.vercel.com/t/design-mode-changes-where-do-i-select-the-design-system/36398.md).
- Output is React code, so handoff is the code itself. Variant/branching UX: not verified.

### Figma Make / Figma AI
- Make kits combine a React package or Figma library with guidelines, so prototypes use production components (https://www.figma.com/blog/introducing-make-kits-and-make-attachments/).
- The Figma agent claims to generate "explore multiple directions" variations using real components and tokens (https://www.figma.com/solutions/ai-design-iteration-generator/, marketing copy).
- Forum failure reports: changes confirmed but not applied, instructions ignored, stuck builds. Users have requested branching/version control for Make (https://forum.figma.com/suggest-a-feature-11/figma-make-structured-version-control-iteration-branching-for-ai-workflows-51303, https://forum.figma.com/report-a-problem-6/figma-make-not-following-even-simple-instructions-updates-not-occurring-46762).

### Magic Patterns
- Infinite canvas. You duplicate a component and prompt for parallel variations, such as four headers in different styles compared side by side. It uses your own tokens and component library (https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/magic-patterns). This is the closest match to the option-board pattern.

### Subframe
- Canvas plus coding agent. Layers map to HTML/React. Components with props, slots and variants sync to the codebase (https://uxmagic.ai/blog/magic-patterns-alternatives). Variant generation for ideation: UNVERIFIED.

### Lovable, Bolt
- Both are full-app builders. Both have click-to-edit layers: Lovable Visual Edits (https://lovable.dev/blog/introducing-visual-edits), and Bolt Visual Edits, which stacks changes and sends them to the model in one batch (https://bolt.new/blog/visual-edits).
- Neither is primarily a divergent-exploration tool.

### Builder.io Visual Copilot / Fusion
- Maps Figma designs to code using your components. Modes are visual, interactive and code (https://builder.io/blog/builder-visual-editor-v2). Focus is hardening, not ideation.

### Uizard, Relume, Tempo
- Uizard (acquired by Miro in 2024): sketch-to-wireframe scanner and Autodesigner (https://uxmagic.ai/blog/magic-patterns-alternatives). Relume is recommended for marketing sites and sitemap/wireframes. Tempo: nothing found. All three are UNVERIFIED.

## Common ideation interaction patterns
1. Parallel variants: duplicate or ask for N options (Magic Patterns, Stitch Ideate, Figma agent, Claude chat).
2. Option board: an infinite canvas where options sit side by side (Stitch, Magic Patterns, Claude canvas).
3. Annotate-and-iterate: pin comments on elements, with a chat fallback for structural changes (Claude, Bolt batched edits).
4. Direct manipulation or sliders for fine tuning (Claude, v0 Design Mode, Lovable, Bolt).
5. Design-system grounding via a registry, kit or ingested repo (v0, Make kits, Claude, Magic Patterns).
6. Branching history is weak or absent. Claude has no version history and Make users request branching. Stitch's agent keeps project memory. Decision logs are essentially not a feature anywhere I found; the chat transcript serves as an implicit log, and it is bundled into the Claude Code handoff.
7. Handoff means an export bundle, code, or MCP.

## Failure modes users report
- Cost: variants burn quota fast.
- Drift over iterations; the fix is a re-anchoring prompt.
- Lost or invisible comments.
- No history, so you cannot return to an earlier option.
- Design-system drift or copies going stale.
- Generic "safe" aesthetics, and options that converge instead of diverging.
- Instructions ignored or unapplied.
- Premature fidelity: ideation tools output production-looking code, which blurs sketch and spec.

## Lessons for Wisp sketch mode
- Make options first-class files, not chat turns. Use a stable ID per option, such as `sketch/<topic>/opt-A`, so there is a durable history even though the tools lack one.
- Render the matrix (option x brand/theme) from tokens. v0 shows per-design-system rendering is feasible and valuable.
- Allow TBDs and use no gates. Mark each option's status (open, parked, chosen, rejected) with a one-line reason. That is the decision log, which no tool provides.
- Prevent drift. Re-derive from an anchor brief on each round, and keep the brief in the sketch file.
- Keep cost visible: cap the default option count at about 3, because tools burn quota on variants.
- Promote path: the chosen option becomes a muse component spec, with TBDs resolved or moved to non_goals and behaviors turned into testable criteria. The sketch carries a `decision_ref`, which matches the existing arch-model and ADR conventions. Handoff bundle idea (Claude Design): ship the chosen option, tokens and the decision log together.
- Keep sketch artifacts visibly low-fidelity, or watermarked, so nobody mistakes them for a spec.

1	# R4: Verifying and hardening agent-built front-end work (researched 2026-10-17)
2	
3	Confidence tags: [P] primary/vendor doc fetched; [S] secondary summary from search snippet only (not opened); [U] unverified/inferred.
4	
5	## 1. Visual verification loops
6	- Anthropic Claude Code best practices [P]: "Give Claude a way to verify its work"; "Claude stops when the work looks done. Without a check it can run, 'looks done' is the only signal." Example for UI: paste a design, "take a screenshot of the result and compare it to the original. list differences and fix them". Wants evidence (screenshot, command output) not assertion. Also: Stop hook as deterministic gate; a fresh-context verification subagent so "the agent doing the work isn't the one grading it"; reviewers prompted for gaps over-report, so restrict to correctness/stated requirements. Failure pattern named: "trust-then-verify gap... If you can't verify it, don't ship it." https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices
7	- Same doc on explore vs plan [P]: plan mode adds overhead; "If you could describe the diff in one sentence, skip the plan"; "Sometimes you should skip planning ... because the task is exploratory." Suggests an interview -> SPEC.md -> fresh session to execute; best specs are self-contained, state out of scope, and "end with an end-to-end verification step".
8	- Playwright MCP [S]: accessibility-snapshot (text) is cheaper than screenshots (~1/4 tokens claimed); hybrid use. Screenshot catches blank regions, CSS collisions, narrow-viewport breaks, contrast, overflow, wrong data bound. https://playwright.dev/docs/getting-started-mcp ; https://qaskills.sh/blog/claude-code-screenshot-frontend-verification-mcp ; https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/08/14/codex-cli-playwright-mcp-browser-automation-accessibility-snapshots-testing/ (GitHub Copilot coding agent has Playwright MCP preconfigured [S]).
9	- Chrome DevTools for agents [S, official domain, snippet only]: agents verify via screenshots, console, and a `lighthouse_audit` tool (a11y/SEO/best-practices, mobile/desktop, navigation/snapshot) against localhost or file://. https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/agents ; https://developer.chrome.com/docs/devtools/agents/use-cases/lighthouse-audit
10	- Cursor [S]: browser tool + Design Mode that hands the agent selected element code, applied CSS, layout, screenshots; lesson: visual evidence as a first-class harness artifact. https://cursor.com/docs/agent/tools/browser ; https://cursor.com/changelog/design-mode-improvements
11	- Anthropic frontend-design plugin [S]: steers against generic "AI slop" aesthetics (aesthetic direction up front). https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/plugins/frontend-design
12	
13	## 2. Storybook / visual regression
14	- Storybook MCP (addon-mcp, Storybook 10.3+) [P]: Development toolset (story previews, interaction tests), Docs toolset (component manifest, props), Testing toolset (`run-story-tests` returns results incl. a11y violations; "self-healing loop"). Caveats: docs toolset needs a components manifest (not all frameworks); "Agents require explicit instructions to avoid hallucinating undocumented properties". https://storybook.js.org/docs/ai/mcp/overview
15	- Chromatic (Storybook team, hosted visual diffs + Storybook MCP), Percy (AI Visual Review Agent filters false positives), Lost Pixel (OSS, Playwright screenshots of stories/pages, baselines in repo, GitHub Action) [S]. https://www.augmentcode.com/guides/visual-regression-testing-ai-generated-uis ; https://momentic.ai/blog/best-visual-regression-testing-tools ; https://percy.io/blog/ai-visual-testing-tools
16	- Key limitation [U/inferred, consistent with sources]: regression tools diff against a baseline; they confirm "unchanged", not "correct". First-time agent output has no baseline, so a human or a rubric must approve the baseline.
17	
18	## 3. Automated a11y
19	- Deque study: axe-core fully covers ~57% of issues by volume (2,000+ audits, 13k pages); remainder needs manual/guided testing [S, official Deque]. https://www.deque.com/blog/automated-testing-study-identifies-57-percent-of-digital-accessibility-issues
20	- Practical pattern: axe via Storybook a11y addon / Playwright, Lighthouse via DevTools MCP, plus explicit probes (computed contrast, target size >=24px per WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 [U: not fetched], focus order via keyboard-driven Playwright run). Absence of axe violations is not evidence of accessibility; gate should report "automated-only" scope.
21	
22	## 4. Design-token linting
23	- Stylelint (e.g. stylelint-declaration-strict-value) fails raw hex/rgb/hsl outside the token sheet; AI "hardcodes the resolved value instead of referencing the semantic token" [S]. https://medium.com/@barshaya97_76274/design-tokens-enforcement-977310b2788e ; https://www.alwaystwisted.com/articles/where-to-lint-design-tokens ; Atlassian token usage guide https://atlassian.design/tokens/use-tokens-in-code/ [S]; "State of AI in Design Systems" coercion techniques https://state-of-ai-in-design-systems.netlify.app/techniques [S, not read].
24	- Pattern: lint (static) + render (visual) are both needed; lint passes can still render wrong.
25	
26	## 5. Vibe coding -> production hardening
27	- Consensus [S]: keep UI/product shape, rebuild foundations; first step is characterization tests pinning current behavior, then refactor, then harden auth/data/integrations. Common failures: interfaces wired only to local state, calls to nonexistent endpoints, saves that don't persist. https://wavect.io/software-development-guide/vibe-coded-prototype-to-production/ ; https://addjam.com/blog/2026-01-12/from-vibe-code-to-production/ ; https://www.vibengineer.io/blog/vibe-coded-prototype-to-production
28	- "Vibe-prototype is your PRD, not your first product version" (Product School/Reforge-style prototype-first) [S]. https://productschool.com/blog/artificial-intelligence/ai-prototyping ; https://www.reforge.com/blog/ai-prototyping-product-development
29	- Spec-first vs code-first: code-first suits uncertain outcomes; "the specification emerges from lessons learned" [S]. https://www.kinde.com/learn/ai-for-software-engineering/best-practice/spec-first-vs-code-first-in-ai-development/
30	
31	## 6. Spec-driven development in practice
32	- Böckeler / Martin Fowler site, Kiro, Spec Kit, Tessl [P via fetch of sdd-3-tools]: Kiro turned a small bug into 4 user stories / 16 acceptance criteria ("sledgehammer to crack a nut"); Spec Kit produced repetitive markdown "repetitive with each other and with the code", review fatigue ("I'd rather review code than all these markdown files"); agents "frequently" ignore instructions or overreach; Tessl showed non-determinism even from detailed specs; spec-as-source risks MDD's "inflexibility and non-determinism"; unclear functional vs technical boundary. https://martinfowler.com/articles/exploring-gen-ai/sdd-3-tools.html
33	- Nothing checks code matches spec; research step catalogued classes then agent regenerated duplicates [S via search summary of same article].
34	- Drift: HN practitioner "specs keep drifting ... duplication and contradictions"; Kiro-style specs treated as launch docs that drift once generation starts [S]. OpenSpec: current specs/ separated from changes/ deltas, brownfield-first, per-change scope reduces churn [S]. https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec ; https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/concepts.md ; https://www.augmentcode.com/guides/spec-driven-development-brownfield-codebases ; https://zenn.dev/cbmrham/articles/202601-spec-driven-development-skepticism?locale=en
35	- When specs help: multi-file, uncertain-approach, well-bounded behavior with checkable outcomes (Anthropic: self-contained, out-of-scope listed, end-to-end verification). When they hurt: small changes, visual/taste-driven work where the "truth" is a rendered artifact, moving design.
36	- Not found: first-party UI-specific SDD write-ups from Shopify/Airbnb/Uber/Atlassian/Vercel on agentic front-end verification. Search returned only Vercel/Shopify commerce-integration material (irrelevant) and Atlassian's token docs. Flag as UNVERIFIED/absent rather than inferring their practice.
37	
38	## 7. Parallel agents on shared UI
39	- Worktrees give file isolation; "merge conflicts" vs "intent conflicts" (clean merge, wrong combined behavior) [S]. Collision hotspots: routing tables, config, component registries (and by extension token files, shared primitives, global CSS). Assign explicit file ownership; sequence tasks that share files; merge one branch at a time; 3-5 agents practical ceiling. https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/git-worktrees-parallel-ai-coding-agents ; https://addyosmani.com/blog/code-agent-orchestra/ ; https://auravcs.com/learn/run-multiple-coding-agents-in-parallel
40	- Anthropic: worktrees, /batch (5-30 subagents each in a worktree), Writer/Reviewer fresh-context pattern [P].
41	- Inference [U]: intent conflicts on UI show up only when rendered together (spacing, z-index, duplicated primitives); needs a post-merge render check, not per-branch checks.
42	
43	## 8. Copy / content truth
44	- AI UI review checklists [S]: invented round numbers (99.9%, 50%), placeholder names (Acme, John Doe), invented testimonials/ratings, missing loading/empty/error/permission states, unlabeled icon buttons, buttons that submit forms by accident. Rule: every finding carries evidence + location (quoted value, where it lives). https://21st.dev/blog/ai-generated-ui-review-checklist ; https://dev.to/janarthanan_soundararajan/what-to-check-when-reviewing-ai-generated-ui-h28 ; https://floneo.co/blog/why-beautiful-ai-generated-uis-still-fail
45	- Mechanizable: extract all visible text from the rendered DOM (Playwright), diff against a source-of-truth copy file/requirement, flag numerals, proper nouns, and claims not traceable to a source.
46	
47	## 9. Failure modes mapped to Wisp (spec -> plan -> implement -> gate, no render, no explore)
48	1. Self-consistency gates never render: spec-gate/plan-challenger/exit-gate judge text. Anthropic's own guidance says the check must return a signal from the running artifact (screenshot, Lighthouse, story tests). Add a "render evidence" artifact (screenshots at defined viewports/themes/states, axe/Lighthouse JSON, console errors) required by the implementation gate for UI scope; gate reports "not rendered" as a coverage gap, never pass.
49	2. Spec churn when design moves: add an explicit explore mode (throwaway prototype, no spec, no gate, time/scope boxed), whose output is a prototype + decision notes; then "spec from prototype" (characterize observable behavior, tokens, states), keeping the prototype as the visual oracle. Use OpenSpec-style change deltas rather than rewriting whole specs; skip the pipeline for one-sentence diffs.
50	3. Spec criteria for taste-based UI should reference a visual oracle (approved screenshot/Storybook story baseline) rather than prose adjectives; regression tools (Chromatic/Lost Pixel/Playwright toHaveScreenshot) then lock it after human approval.
51	4. Copy truth: add a content-provenance check (rendered text vs source copy; flag invented stats/testimonials/placeholders).
52	5. Token compliance: lint (stylelint strict-value) as deterministic check in smith verification; render check for effective computed values.
53	6. A11y: run axe + keyboard + contrast + target-size probes; verdict wording must say automated coverage is partial (~57% per Deque).
54	7. Parallel agents: file-ownership declared in plan; shared primitives/token files single-writer; integrated render check after merge (intent conflicts).
55	8. Independent verifier with fresh context, evidence-bearing, scoped to correctness (Anthropic), already matches Wisp's adversary/exit-gate shape but lacks rendering tools.
56	
57	## Unverified / gaps
58	- Most Playwright/Chromatic/Percy/Lost Pixel/parallel-agent claims are from search summaries, not opened pages.
59	- WCAG 2.2 target-size threshold not fetched.
60	- No primary sources found for Shopify/Airbnb/Uber/Atlassian/Vercel agentic front-end verification practices.
61	- Prototype-to-spec has no strong primary source; evidence is blog-level.

- "Vibe-prototype is your PRD, not your first product version" (Product School/Reforge-style prototype-first) [S]. https://productschool.com/blog/artificial-intelligence/ai-prototyping ; https://www.reforge.com/blog/ai-prototyping-product-development
- Spec-first vs code-first: code-first suits uncertain outcomes; "the specification emerges from lessons learned" [S]. https://www.kinde.com/learn/ai-for-software-engineering/best-practice/spec-first-vs-code-first-in-ai-development/

## 6. Spec-driven development in practice
- Böckeler / Martin Fowler site, Kiro, Spec Kit, Tessl [P via fetch of sdd-3-tools]: Kiro turned a small bug into 4 user stories / 16 acceptance criteria ("sledgehammer to crack a nut"); Spec Kit produced repetitive markdown "repetitive with each other and with the code", review fatigue ("I'd rather review code than all these markdown files"); agents "frequently" ignore instructions or overreach; Tessl showed non-determinism even from detailed specs; spec-as-source risks MDD's "inflexibility and non-determinism"; unclear functional vs technical boundary. https://martinfowler.com/articles/exploring-gen-ai/sdd-3-tools.html
- Nothing checks code matches spec; research step catalogued classes then agent regenerated duplicates [S via search summary of same article].
- Drift: HN practitioner "specs keep drifting ... duplication and contradictions"; Kiro-style specs treated as launch docs that drift once generation starts [S]. OpenSpec: current specs/ separated from changes/ deltas, brownfield-first, per-change scope reduces churn [S]. https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec ; https://github.com/Fission-AI/OpenSpec/blob/main/docs/concepts.md ; https://www.augmentcode.com/guides/spec-driven-development-brownfield-codebases ; https://zenn.dev/cbmrham/articles/202601-spec-driven-development-skepticism?locale=en
- When specs help: multi-file, uncertain-approach, well-bounded behavior with checkable outcomes (Anthropic: self-contained, out-of-scope listed, end-to-end verification). When they hurt: small changes, visual/taste-driven work where the "truth" is a rendered artifact, moving design.
- Not found: first-party UI-specific SDD write-ups from Shopify/Airbnb/Uber/Atlassian/Vercel on agentic front-end verification. Search returned only Vercel/Shopify commerce-integration material (irrelevant) and Atlassian's token docs. Flag as UNVERIFIED/absent rather than inferring their practice.

## 7. Parallel agents on shared UI
- Worktrees give file isolation; "merge conflicts" vs "intent conflicts" (clean merge, wrong combined behavior) [S]. Collision hotspots: routing tables, config, component registries (and by extension token files, shared primitives, global CSS). Assign explicit file ownership; sequence tasks that share files; merge one branch at a time; 3-5 agents practical ceiling. https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/git-worktrees-parallel-ai-coding-agents ; https://addyosmani.com/blog/code-agent-orchestra/ ; https://auravcs.com/learn/run-multiple-coding-agents-in-parallel
- Anthropic: worktrees, /batch (5-30 subagents each in a worktree), Writer/Reviewer fresh-context pattern [P].
- Inference [U]: intent conflicts on UI show up only when rendered together (spacing, z-index, duplicated primitives); needs a post-merge render check, not per-branch checks.

## 8. Copy / content truth
- AI UI review checklists [S]: invented round numbers (99.9%, 50%), placeholder names (Acme, John Doe), invented testimonials/ratings, missing loading/empty/error/permission states, unlabeled icon buttons, buttons that submit forms by accident. Rule: every finding carries evidence + location (quoted value, where it lives). https://21st.dev/blog/ai-generated-ui-review-checklist ; https://dev.to/janarthanan_soundararajan/what-to-check-when-reviewing-ai-generated-ui-h28 ; https://floneo.co/blog/why-beautiful-ai-generated-uis-still-fail
- Mechanizable: extract all visible text from the rendered DOM (Playwright), diff against a source-of-truth copy file/requirement, flag numerals, proper nouns, and claims not traceable to a source.

## 9. Failure modes mapped to Wisp (spec -> plan -> implement -> gate, no render, no explore)
1. Self-consistency gates never render: spec-gate/plan-challenger/exit-gate judge text. Anthropic's own guidance says the check must return a signal from the running artifact (screenshot, Lighthouse, story tests). Add a "render evidence" artifact (screenshots at defined viewports/themes/states, axe/Lighthouse JSON, console errors) required by the implementation gate for UI scope; gate reports "not rendered" as a coverage gap, never pass.
2. Spec churn when design moves: add an explicit explore mode (throwaway prototype, no spec, no gate, time/scope boxed), whose output is a prototype + decision notes; then "spec from prototype" (characterize observable behavior, tokens, states), keeping the prototype as the visual oracle. Use OpenSpec-style change deltas rather than rewriting whole specs; skip the pipeline for one-sentence diffs.
3. Spec criteria for taste-based UI should reference a visual oracle (approved screenshot/Storybook story baseline) rather than prose adjectives; regression tools (Chromatic/Lost Pixel/Playwright toHaveScreenshot) then lock it after human approval.
4. Copy truth: add a content-provenance check (rendered text vs source copy; flag invented stats/testimonials/placeholders).
5. Token compliance: lint (stylelint strict-value) as deterministic check in smith verification; render check for effective computed values.
6. A11y: run axe + keyboard + contrast + target-size probes; verdict wording must say automated coverage is partial (~57% per Deque).
7. Parallel agents: file-ownership declared in plan; shared primitives/token files single-writer; integrated render check after merge (intent conflicts).
8. Independent verifier with fresh context, evidence-bearing, scoped to correctness (Anthropic), already matches Wisp's adversary/exit-gate shape but lacks rendering tools.

## Unverified / gaps
- Most Playwright/Chromatic/Percy/Lost Pixel/parallel-agent claims are from search summaries, not opened pages.
- WCAG 2.2 target-size threshold not fetched.
- No primary sources found for Shopify/Airbnb/Uber/Atlassian/Vercel agentic front-end verification practices.
- Prototype-to-spec has no strong primary source; evidence is blog-level.

## (1) CONTRADICTIONS between sources (and with the WP draft)

1. Code Connect numbers: R2 blog median (quality +1, tokens -29.5%, duration -19.6%) vs search snippet Coinbase 11.5%/22.3%/22.5% (R2-17 vs R2-18). Different cohorts/sources; do not quote either without opening the Figma blog.
2. get_variable_defs: desktop-only (search summary) vs not remote-only (official table) (R2-06). Prefer the official table; verify.
3. Storybook MCP tool names: R1 lists docs-list/docs-show/get-storybook-story-instructions/test-run; R4 lists toolsets with `run-story-tests` (R1-33 vs R4-18). One may be an older/LLM-summarised name set; check docs/ai/mcp/overview.
4. Screenshots: R2-26 says screenshots alone drift and need structured data; R4 recommends screenshot loops as the check. Resolve: screenshots are evidence of rendering only, specification must come from tokens/structure (R1 lesson 2) plus a11y tree (R4-12).
5. Parallel ceiling: 3-5 agents practical (R4-55) vs Anthropic /batch 5-30 subagents (R4-56). The latter is capability, the former is practitioner advice for merge-safety; WP-55's "3-5" needs qualification.
6. Reviewer scope: Anthropic says over-prompted reviewers over-report, restrict to correctness (R4-06); WP-50 says scanners report all with confidence then filter separately. Compatible only if the filter stage is separate and cheap; test in WP-60.
7. Option count: R3 lesson says cap ~3 (R3-63); WP-16 says propose ~4 directions. Pick one default (suggest 3 for options within a direction, 4 only for first direction-commit) and justify in the ADR.
8. Spec drift: R1-39 says OpenSpec specs drift and do not self-update; R4-48 says OpenSpec per-change deltas reduce churn. Both can hold (reduces churn, does not solve drift).
9. uSpec agents: blog says Cursor; docs say Cursor/Claude Code/Codex (R1-17).
10. R3-49 "decision logs are not a feature anywhere" vs R3-21 Stitch agent remembers project history and R3-09 handoff bundle includes chat. Memory exists; structured, status-bearing logs not found. Absence-of-evidence claim, weak.
11. Kiro: vendor claims browser-verified UI loop (R1-37) vs Fowler review finding over-specification and no code-vs-spec check (R4-39, R4-45). Not directly contradictory; vendor claim is unverified.
12. WP-30 "no TBD in spec" vs R3 "allow TBDs" in sketch: consistent only if sketch and spec are strictly separate artifacts; enforce by schema (sketch not a spec@N).
13. R3-13 multi-person editing unreliable vs Wisp's file-based multi-agent model: not a contradiction, but note single-author assumption.
